content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "missing_justification", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quoted sentences appear in the text (separated by one sentence: \"Need to prove best response for Xiang among all allowed splits is indeed to split each big once... We tested n=2 case where splitting one big into 3 gave larger Liu share.\"), and mean what the objection says. The only rigorous computation in the write-up is the parity/cancellation argument for the multiset {d+\u03b4_i, d-\u03b4_i} \u222a {d}, i.e. exactly the case where each 2d piece receives exactly one cut. For Xiang responses that split some piece into 3+ parts, or use fewer than n cuts, the text offers only two n=2 numerical examples (0.7 > 0.6, and 0.6) and then explicitly writes \"Need to prove...\". Nowhere else in the text is this case handled. Hence the lower bound (L) is not established for all n; the step is essential to the claimed guarantee."}
